help.title: Usage Guide
help.bind.step1: 1. Open the target app (e.g. a screenshot tool) and start its hotkey recorder — it will ask you to press a key.
help.bind.step2: 2. Switch back to MultiTapKey and click the Test button of the gesture you want (e.g. "Test Long").
help.bind.step3: 3. Switch back to the target app — it will record the output key of that gesture (e.g. F5).
help.bind.note: Why not just hold the mouse button to record? The mouse hardware sends F24 at the instant you press it, and the target app sees F24 immediately — this is a system-level behavior that cannot be intercepted. So we do it the other way around: let the app record the key that MultiTapKey emits.
help.section.mouse: Make the mouse work without G HUB (on-board memory)
help.mouse.step1: 1. In Logitech G HUB, assign the mouse button to F24.
help.mouse.step2: 2. Turn on On-Board Memory Mode and save the profile to the mouse.
help.mouse.step3: 3. After that, the mouse works even when G HUB is closed.
help.tips.text: If the target app ignores program-sent keys, try this: press and hold the mouse button first, then open the recorder — after the long-press threshold, MultiTapKey will emit the output key.
